title: Build Reliable Claude API Workflows
summary: Integrate the Claude Messages API with environment-based credentials, explicit request contracts, state ownership, validation, observability, and bounded recovery.
objectives: Explain the Messages API request, response, content-block, and conversation-state contracts.
Use official SDKs with environment-based credentials and configurable model identifiers.
Validate outputs and handle stop reasons, rate limits, timeouts, and uncertain outcomes explicitly.
Record safe operational evidence without logging secrets or sensitive prompt content.

sections.title: Messages are structured and application-managed
paragraphs: A Messages API request identifies a model, output budget, prior user and assistant turns, and optional system instructions, tools, or other controls. Responses contain typed content blocks, usage, and a stop reason. Do not assume that every response is one prose string. In production environments, engineers must account for token utilization patterns, context window pressure, and deterministic execution boundaries. When system constraints or rate limits are approached, explicit retry strategies with exponential backoff and jitter prevent cascading failures across downstream dependencies.

The application owns conversational state. For a continued exchange, preserve the required prior turns and send them again according to the current API contract. Define retention, truncation, summarization, privacy, and deletion behavior as application policies rather than accidental side effects. In production environments, engineers must account for token utilization patterns, context window pressure, and deterministic execution boundaries. When system constraints or rate limits are approached, explicit retry strategies with exponential backoff and jitter prevent cascading failures across downstream dependencies.
sections.callout: The system instruction is a top-level request field in the Messages API, not a system-role item in the messages array.

sections.title: Keep credentials and volatile choices in configuration
paragraphs: Load the API key from the runtime environment or a managed secret store. Fail closed when it is unavailable, keep it out of prompts and logs, scope access to the workload, and use an operational process for rotation and revocation. In production environments, engineers must account for token utilization patterns, context window pressure, and deterministic execution boundaries. When system constraints or rate limits are approached, explicit retry strategies with exponential backoff and jitter prevent cascading failures across downstream dependencies.

Treat model identifiers, output budgets, timeouts, retry policy, and region or deployment choices as reviewed configuration. Verify currently supported values from official documentation and avoid baking an unverified model name into reusable learning code. sections.title: Validate the response contract
paragraphs: Inspect content-block types and stop reasons before consuming output. A normal end turn, output-budget stop, tool request, refusal, pause, and transport failure imply different next actions. Never concatenate unknown blocks into trusted application data. In production environments, engineers must account for token utilization patterns, context window pressure, and deterministic execution boundaries. When system constraints or rate limits are approached, explicit retry strategies with exponential backoff and jitter prevent cascading failures across downstream dependencies.

Validate required fields, allowed values, lengths, citations, and business rules at the application boundary. When downstream code needs structured intent, use an explicit structured interface and schema rather than recovering a decision from free-form prose. In production environments, engineers must account for token utilization patterns, context window pressure, and deterministic execution boundaries. When system constraints or rate limits are approached, explicit retry strategies with exponential backoff and jitter prevent cascading failures across downstream dependencies.

sections.title: Recover with bounds and reconciliation
paragraphs: Classify failures before retrying. A transient availability or rate-limit response may be retried with provider guidance, jitter, a maximum attempt count, and an end-to-end deadline. Authentication, authorization, malformed requests, and validation failures require correction rather than unchanged retry. In production environments, engineers must account for token utilization patterns, context window pressure, and deterministic execution boundaries. When system constraints or rate limits are approached, explicit retry strategies with exponential backoff and jitter prevent cascading failures across downstream dependencies.

A timed-out read-only request can often be retried safely. A timeout surrounding an external side effect has an unknown outcome until the system of record is reconciled. Use idempotency or operation identifiers in your own workflow and verify postconditions before repeating an action. In production environments, engineers must account for token utilization patterns, context window pressure, and deterministic execution boundaries. When system constraints or rate limits are approached, explicit retry strategies with exponential backoff and jitter prevent cascading failures across downstream dependencies.

sections.title: Observe the workflow without leaking data
paragraphs: Record a request or trace identifier, application and prompt version, configured model reference, latency, usage, stop reason, retry count, validation result, and final workflow state. These fields support evaluation, cost analysis, incident response, and rollback decisions. In production environments, engineers must account for token utilization patterns, context window pressure, and deterministic execution boundaries. When system constraints or rate limits are approached, explicit retry strategies with exponential backoff and jitter prevent cascading failures across downstream dependencies.

Do not log API keys, authorization headers, raw secrets, or unrestricted prompt and response bodies. Use data classification, redaction, access control, retention limits, and sampled or derived metrics appropriate to the workload. activity.title: Design a production-shaped Claude API client
instructions: Define a request contract with configurable model reference, output budget, system instruction, messages, timeout, and trace identifier; load credentials only from an environment or managed secret boundary.
Define handlers for text and non-text content blocks plus end-turn, output-budget, tool-use, refusal or pause, rate-limit, authentication, validation, timeout, and server-failure outcomes.
Create deterministic tests with synthetic responses for a successful answer, truncated output, malformed block, retryable failure, non-retryable failure, and uncertain side-effect outcome.
Write a telemetry allowlist and redaction policy, then demonstrate one trace that proves behavior without exposing prompt content or credentials.
evidence: A secret-free client design or implementation with typed request and response handling, bounded retries, reconciliation, and deterministic tests.
A telemetry example and policy showing request correlation, versions, latency, usage, stop reason, validation, retry, and terminal state without sensitive values.
activity.reflectionPrompt: Which failure in your client requires reconciliation rather than retry, and what evidence proves the real outcome?

cues.text: Treat Messages requests and responses as typed contracts while your application deliberately owns conversation state and retention.
Load secrets from an operational boundary and keep model references, budgets, timeouts, and retry policies in reviewed configuration.
Inspect every content-block type and stop reason, then validate structure and business rules before downstream use.
Retry only transient failures within a budget and reconcile unknown side effects before any repeated action.
Capture correlation, versions, latency, usage, stop reasons, retries, validation, and terminal state without logging secrets or unrestricted content.
Move one request through configuration, send, typed response parsing, validation, recovery decision, and terminal evidence.
cues.accessibilityAlternative: A static state table lists configuration, send, parse, validate, recover, and terminal-evidence stages with inputs and allowed outcomes.

cues.text: Ask learners why an authentication failure and a rate-limit response require different handling.
Allow three minutes to remove sensitive fields from a sample log while preserving diagnostic value.
Check that every terminal path is bounded, observable, validated, and free of credential values.
Guide the client contract, outcome handlers, deterministic fixtures, telemetry allowlist, and reconciliation evidence.
Begin the check after the learner can explain state, validation, retries, reconciliation, and safe telemetry.

questions.prompt: Who owns multi-turn conversation state for a Messages API workflow?
choices: The application using the API
The model name
The user's browser cache in every deployment
No component
questions.explanation: The application deliberately preserves, transforms, retains, and resends the conversation state required by its workflow.

questions.prompt: Where should a reusable application obtain its model identifier?
choices: From a hard-coded tutorial value forever
From the API key
From reviewed configuration verified against current official documentation
From the response text
questions.explanation: Model identifiers and support are volatile and should be configurable and source-verified.

questions.prompt: What should happen when the response has an unhandled stop reason?
choices: Treat it as a successful end turn
Enter an explicit non-success path and preserve diagnostic evidence
Discard the response and retry forever
Concatenate every block into trusted text
questions.explanation: Each stop reason is part of the response contract and needs deliberate handling.

questions.prompt: Which failure should not be retried unchanged?
choices: A transient provider failure within the retry budget
A provider-directed rate limit with retry guidance
A connection reset before a read-only response
An authentication or request-validation failure
questions.explanation: Deterministic authentication and validation errors require corrected authority or input.

questions.prompt: Which telemetry set is safest and most useful by default?
choices: API keys and full authorization headers
Every raw prompt and response with indefinite retention
Correlation, versions, latency, usage, stop reason, retry, validation, and terminal state under an allowlist
No telemetry for any production workflow
questions.explanation: Allowlisted operational metadata supports diagnosis while avoiding secrets and unrestricted content.
